focus.label: Make room for the buyer
focus.explanation: It needed work in 4 of the last 4 calls on this skill.
focus.why_it_matters: The buyer needs a clear way to decide and an answer that fits what they asked.
focus.selected_reason: It needed work on this call.
focus.verdict: After one relevant feature, ask the buyer what would change in their workflow and wait for the answer.

evidence.quote: Let me finish the full explanation first. With Business Cash-Flow Review, we begin with an introduction, then a detailed discussion of the delivery sequence. The included scope is cash-flow mapping, scenario review and a written operating plan. We also prepare a kickoff note, collect your requirements, arrange a working session, record the responsibilities, and review progress with the coordinator. There are several useful points I want to cover before you ask anything: preparation, communication, documentation, the delivery calendar, review expectations, escalation and handover. Each point helps the team understand the process. I know you have a question, but if I explain all the stages together it will save time later. We have a structured way of discussing the starting point, the work in progress, the first review, the next review and the final acceptance. The coordinator gets a summary, the manager sees open items, and everyone knows that a question can be raised. The next part is how we organise the first conversation and how we write the review note. Then I can explain the sequence once more from the buyer’s point of view, because there are a lot of details and I want you to hear them all before we move on.
evidence.observation: Said by Mira Nivsekar, the seller.

evidence.quote: Hold on, I have one specific question before you explain the whole package.
evidence.observation: Said by Viren Kovirakar, the buyer.

root_cause.hypothesis: Thinking a full explanation is a useful one.
alternatives: Time pressure or missing context could also explain it.
